What VerseKit does for you in Star Citizen

Every slot of your ship

The hangar shows every slot of your ship: turret and weapons, rack and missiles, mining head and modules. VerseKit reads them from the game data of your installation. You fit each slot on its own, parts built into the ship show without a choice.

Share a loadout as a code for Discord or as a file. When you paste one, you see first what arrives. Ships move between Planned and My hangar with their loadout, name and note. Hover a ship's name and a small window shows speed, size, cargo and buy price.

The info bar over the game

A narrow bar right over the game: your shard and, if you like, your FPS, the server FPS and the players on shard and server, plus the last hit of the ore scanner. Movable, in a size of its own, visible without the game running too.

VerseKit reads the values from the game picture. They stay on your computer.

Who is behind a handle?

Type a handle or org into the info bar, press Enter: name, organizations, rank and profile, without leaving the game. Alt+Shift+H puts you straight into the search field. A click on an organization lists its members.

Mark handles and orgs as friendly, neutral, hostile or watched. The Relations tab shows every mark in one place, with export and import. An org can share its list at an https address, in the sc-social-overlay format too. “Load list” fetches it and keeps your own marks.

Blueprint tracker: new blueprints in seconds

Unlock a blueprint and it is in the list at once. VerseKit reads the game's own logs, without touching the game itself.

The overlay shows it right on top of the game: a narrow window, always on top, and it can let clicks pass through. When you leave an armistice zone, it says “weapons free”.

Contracts that bring you blueprints

In game, every contract shows which blueprints it hands out and which of those you are still missing. Without tabbing out.

Crafting: ingredients, times, prices

Ingredients, amounts, crafting time and price for every item, and whether you have the blueprint. “For ship” shows only parts that fit one of your ships. Enter what runs at the fabricator: VerseKit counts down the time left and tells you when it is done.

Mining and refining

Locations and concentration per material, plus a refinery comparison per ore. On Windows, Alt+Shift+R reads the refinery terminal, in the German game too. If the station is surely in the list of places, it becomes your storage location. Yield, speed and cost of the nine methods come from the game data.

Translation for every channel

German, French, Spanish, Bavarian, Dutch and more, set apart for LIVE, HOTFIX, PTU, EPTU and Tech Preview. If another program overwrites your choice, VerseKit puts it back.

My inventory, with purchases and sales from the game

Materials, goods and items in one place. What you buy or sell in a shop, VerseKit suggests from the log for you to book. After a patch, “Move home” takes everything to your new home location.

Shopping list from the shops

Parts from the shops go into one list with their amount, per ship, with a total and a ready shopping route. If a part is sold in a system you fly to anyway, the route stays there. Set a ship to Ready and VerseKit offers to tick off its open items.

Trading with real profit

Shops, sell locations and routes that tell you what is left at the end. Not just what something costs. Pick a location to see its shops, one click shows everything a shop sells with its price. The Cartel Bank shows your accounts and bookings and takes your requests.

Your statistics

Play time, ships, contracts, quantum jumps, crashes and injuries, counted from your game logs. They are kept even after the game deletes the logs.

Your look, your controls

Six colour schemes and any size you like. Plus: see which stick has which number. Under Axes & curves you set dead zone and curve per axis, with a large preview.

What VerseKit writes into the game

VerseKit adds what the game's own texts leave out. Class, size and grade sit right next to a component's name. Every contract shows which blueprints it hands out, and below an item's description you see whether you already have its blueprint. Weapons and components show their stats there too, to compare before you buy. Each part can be switched off, and “Remove again” restores the original texts character for character.
